# Kruskal-wallis {#sec-kruskal}

{{< include ../preamble.qmd >}}

## Concepts and intuitions {.unnumbered}

## Formal {.unnumbered}

$$
    H = (N - 1) \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^g n_i(\bar{r_{i.}} - \bar{r})^2}{\sum_{i = 1}^g \sum_{j = 1}^{n_i} (r_{ij} - \bar{r})^2}
$${#eq-kruskal}

## Examples {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Kruskal-Wallis Test Analysis"
#| label: fig-kruskal-analysis

# Create sample data with multiple groups
set.seed(789)
group_a <- rnorm(30, mean = 50, sd = 5)
group_b <- rnorm(30, mean = 55, sd = 5)
group_c <- rnorm(30, mean = 52, sd = 5)

# Combine into a data frame
kw_data <- data.frame(
  values = c(group_a, group_b, group_c),
  group = rep(c("Group A", "Group B", "Group C"), each = 30)
)

# Run Kruskal-Wallis test (non-parametric alternative to ANOVA)
kw_result <- kruskal.test(values ~ group, data = kw_data)
print("Kruskal-Wallis Test Result:")
print(kw_result)

# Interpretation:
# If p-value > 0.05: we fail to reject H0 (group distributions are not significantly different)
# If p-value < 0.05: we reject H0 (at least one group distribution is significantly different)

# Get descriptive statistics by group (using median instead of mean for non-parametric data)
print("\nDescriptive Statistics by Group:")
print(aggregate(values ~ group, data = kw_data, FUN = function(x) c(median = median(x), sd = sd(x), n = length(x))))
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Kruskal-Wallis Visualizations: Boxplot and Group Medians"
#| label: fig-kruskal-plots

# Set up 1x2 panel layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Panel 1: Boxplot
boxplot(values ~ group, data = kw_data,
        main = "Boxplot: Distribution by Group",
        xlab = "Group",
        ylab = "Values",
        col = c("lightblue", "lightcoral", "lightgreen"),
        border = "black",
        lwd = 1.5)

# Panel 2: Group medians with interquartile range
group_medians <- aggregate(values ~ group, data = kw_data, FUN = median)
group_q1 <- aggregate(values ~ group, data = kw_data, FUN = function(x) quantile(x, 0.25))
group_q3 <- aggregate(values ~ group, data = kw_data, FUN = function(x) quantile(x, 0.75))

plot(1:3, group_medians$values,
     main = "Group Medians with Interquartile Range",
     xlab = "Group",
     ylab = "Median Values",
     ylim = c(min(group_q1$values), max(group_q3$values)),
     pch = 19,
     cex = 1.5,
     col = c("blue", "red", "green"),
     xaxt = "n")
axis(1, at = 1:3, labels = c("Group A", "Group B", "Group C"))

# Add IQR error bars
for (i in 1:3) {
  segments(i, group_q1$values[i], 
           i, group_q3$values[i],
           lwd = 2, col = c("blue", "red", "green")[i])
  segments(i - 0.05, group_q1$values[i],
           i + 0.05, group_q1$values[i],
           lwd = 2, col = c("blue", "red", "green")[i])
  segments(i - 0.05, group_q3$values[i],
           i + 0.05, group_q3$values[i],
           lwd = 2, col = c("blue", "red", "green")[i])
}

# Reset plot layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Kruskal-Wallis Visualizations: Violin Plot and Stripchart"
#| label: fig-kruskal-distribution

# Set up 1x2 panel layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Panel 1: Boxplot with overlaid points (stripchart)
boxplot(values ~ group, data = kw_data,
        main = "Boxplot with Data Points",
        xlab = "Group",
        ylab = "Values",
        col = c("lightblue", "lightcoral", "lightgreen"),
        border = "black",
        lwd = 1.5)

# Add jittered points to show individual observations
set.seed(100)
for (i in 1:3) {
  group_data <- kw_data$values[kw_data$group == c("Group A", "Group B", "Group C")[i]]
  x_pos <- rep(i, length(group_data)) + rnorm(length(group_data), 0, 0.04)
  points(x_pos, group_data, pch = 16, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.3), cex = 0.7)
}

# Panel 2: Density plot overlay
plot(density(group_a), main = "Density Plot by Group",
     xlab = "Values", ylab = "Density",
     col = "blue", lwd = 2, xlim = c(35, 70))
lines(density(group_b), col = "red", lwd = 2)
lines(density(group_c), col = "green", lwd = 2)
legend("topright", 
       legend = c("Group A", "Group B", "Group C"),
       col = c("blue", "red", "green"),
       lwd = 2,
       cex = 0.8)

# Reset plot layout
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```
